newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais says IMF loan less important now.
newsitem.headline: Chubais says IMF loan less important now.

text.p: Russia's economic policy chief said on Thursday that loans from the International Monetary Fund were far less important to Russia today than two years ago, as Russia can now raise funds on international capital markets.
"Today the IMF loans do not play even a fifth of the role for Russia which they played two years ago," First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais told reporters.
"The IMF loans continue to remain cheap... But in principle we can borrow money for a slightly higher price on the European, private markets," said Chubais, who is also Finance Minister.
"Private investors recognise today that we are a reliable country, and our room for manoeuvre has widened sharply."

The IMF has effectively suspended a $10 billion three-year loan to Russia, mainly because tax receipts are running far below budgeted levels, threatening to undermine government finances, re-ignite inflation and stifle nascent growth.
An IMF mission is currently in Moscow for final talks on a 1997 economic programme which could pave the way for a resumption of payments of the Extended Fund Facility loan.

IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said earlier this month he was ready to recommend that the IMF board approve the 1997 plan, but the Russian government must first submit a new tax code to parliament.

Chubais said he did not intend to discuss either the delayed tranches of the IMF loan or the 1997 programme when he visits Washington at the end of this week for the spring meetings of the IMF and World Bank.

"The main negotiations were held here during the visit of Camdessus. Now there is an IMF mission here and the final technical details are in the process of being worked out. Frankly, I am not concerned," he said.
Russia has budgeted credits $3.65 billion from the IMF under the EFF this year.
It has also brought forward plans to return to international capital markets, after a successful two billion mark Eurobond in March following last November's debut $1 billion Eurobond.
Chubais said last week that Russia had mandated investment banks JP Morgan and SBC Warburg to lead a new dollar Eurobond in the next few months.
Officials say there will be at least one other Eurobond this year.
